# K-means in R (first look)

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| eval: false

library(tidyverse) # Load core tidyverse packages

# Preview the iris dataset
iris |> head(n = 2)

# Plot sepal length vs sepal width, colored by species
ggplot(iris, aes(x = Sepal.Length, y = Sepal.Width, color = factor(Species))) +
  geom_point(size = 3) + # add points
  theme_minimal() +      # use minimal theme
  labs(color = "Cluster") # customize legend title
```

------------------------------------------------------------------------

# K-means in R (clustering)

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| eval: false

library(tidymodels); library(tidyverse)

# Remove species column (we want unsupervised clustering)
data <- iris |> select(-Species)
  
# Apply K-means clustering with k = 3 (scale first)
kmeans_fit <- kmeans(scale(data), centers = 3)

# Add cluster assignments and true species back to data
data <- data |> 
  mutate(Cluster = kmeans_fit$cluster,
         Species = iris$Species)

# Visualize clustering result
ggplot(data, aes(x = Sepal.Length, y = Sepal.Width, color = factor(Cluster))) +
  geom_point(size = 3) +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(color = "Cluster")
```

------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Random forest in R

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| eval: false

library(tidymodels)

# Split iris data into training (80%) and testing (20%) sets
set.seed(123)
data_split <- initial_split(iris |> select(-Species), prop = 0.8)
train <- training(data_split)
test <- testing(data_split)

# Define recipe (Petal.Length is the outcome, others are predictors)
rf_recipe <- recipe(Petal.Length ~ ., data = train)

# Specify random forest model (500 trees, permutation importance)
rf_model <- rand_forest(trees = 500) |> 
  set_engine("ranger", importance = "permutation") |> 
  set_mode("regression")
```

------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Training the random forest

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| eval: false

# Create workflow combining recipe and model
rf_wf <- workflow() |> 
  add_recipe(rf_recipe) |> 
  add_model(rf_model)

# Fit model on training data
rf_fit <- rf_wf |> fit(data = train)

# Predict on test set
rf_preds <- predict(rf_fit, test) |> bind_cols(test)
```

------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Evaluating performance

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| eval: false

# Compute regression metrics: RMSE, R², MAE
rf_preds |> metrics(truth = Petal.Length, estimate = .pred)
```

------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Variable importance

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| eval: false

library(vip)

# Extract fitted model and visualize top predictors
rf_fit |> extract_fit_parsnip() |> vip(num_features = 3)
```

------------------------------------------------------------------------

# tidymodels workflow

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| eval: false

library(tidymodels)

# Example: linear regression model for Petal.Length
# Define recipe (preprocessing)
lm_recipe <- recipe(Petal.Length ~ Sepal.Length + Sepal.Width, data = iris)

# Define model
lm_model <- linear_reg() |> set_engine("lm")

# Combine recipe + model into a workflow
lm_wf <- workflow() |> 
  add_recipe(lm_recipe) |> 
  add_model(lm_model)
```

------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Resampling with rsample

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| eval: false

# Create 5-fold cross-validation splits
set.seed(123)
cv_folds <- vfold_cv(iris, v = 5)

cv_folds
```

------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Hyperparameter tuning with tune

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| eval: false

# Define random forest model with hyperparameters to tune
rf_tune <- rand_forest(mtry = tune(), trees = 500, min_n = tune()) |> 
  set_engine("ranger") |> 
  set_mode("regression")

# Define grid of candidate values
rf_grid <- grid_regular(mtry(range = c(1,4)), min_n(), levels = 3)

# Run grid search with cross-validation
rf_tuned <- tune_grid(
  workflow() |> add_recipe(rf_recipe) |> add_model(rf_tune),
  resamples = cv_folds,
  grid = rf_grid
)
```
